stem:
Pihu wants a fair comparison of vinegar and soap water using one prepared red-cabbage extract as the indicator. The two liquids start with different colours. She has a dropper and will record each final colour.

Which plan makes that comparison fair?

options.text: Use the same cabbage extract for both, add comparable dropper amounts of each liquid, and record both final colours.
Use one drop of vinegar and ten drops of soap water; the test is still fair if the indicator is the same.
If both liquids can later be labelled acid or base, the comparison must have been fair no matter how it was done.
Different starting colours of vinegar and soap water make any comparison unfair, even if final colours are recorded clearly.

teacher.key_rationale: A fair indicator test uses the same extract, comparable amounts, and recorded final colours. Unequal amounts, judging fairness only from later labels, or blaming starting colours alone are wrong.
